body.title: Unit-test the reconcileConfig contract
body.summary: Add src/config/__tests__/config-reconcile.test.ts (node:test + node:assert/strict, kebab-case sibling naming) covering the full pure contract with in-memory fixtures driven through the injectable `catalog` parameter — no on-disk fixture is needed at this level because the reconciler is pure. Cover: carried/filled/repaired classification; falsy-but-valid values (false, 0, "", [], {}) carried and never filled; null at a non-nullable declared type repaired; a type-matching object with extra un-enumerated sub-keys carried whole without recursion; the t2 captured document surviving a gained-and-lost-keys catalog with all three dynamic namespaces deep-equal; a catalog key reconciled beside a dynamic sibling at the same level with independent outcomes; the changed-derivation invariant; idempotence across the whole fixture corpus; non-object roots; empty and non-matching catalogs; partially-present ancestor chains (intermediates synthesized, only the leaf recorded in filled); scalar/array ancestor collision recording the CATALOG path in repaired together with the discarded scalar value; a value already equal to the catalog default recorded as carried not filled; both ConfigCatalogError throw cases asserted by class and by the path they name; and non-mutation via a deep-freeze helper.
acceptanceChecks: src/config/__tests__/config-reconcile.test.ts exists and all 18 named subjects from the test strategy have a corresponding assertion

The captured t2 fixture reconciles with models.analyze.roleTiers, models.analyze.byRepo and models.agents deep-equal to the baseline, against a catalog that both gained and lost rows relative to the fixture
The two catalog-integrity failures are asserted to be instances of ConfigCatalogError and to carry the offending catalog path, and no user-config input in the corpus produces that class
The ancestor-collision test asserts the discarded scalar value is present in the repair record, not just the path
A deep-freeze helper is used to prove `existing` is never mutated
`npx tsx --test 'src/config/__tests__/*.test.ts'` passes with no new dependency added to package.json

tests.name: catalog key absent from existing → default written, path in filled
catalog key present and type-valid → value carried unchanged and referentially preserved for objects/arrays
catalog key present but type-invalid → catalog default substituted, path in repaired
falsy-but-valid values (false, 0, "", [], {}) carried, never filled — existence via hasOwnProperty, not truthiness
null at a non-nullable declared type is repaired, not carried
type-matching object with extra un-enumerated sub-keys carried whole, no recursion to prune
dynamic namespaces roleTiers / byRepo / agents deep-equal across a gained-and-lost-keys catalog on the t2 captured fixture
catalog key reconciled beside a dynamic sibling at the same level — outcomes independent
changed === (filled.length + repaired.length > 0) and changed === false implies config deep-equals existing
idempotence — reconcileConfig(reconcileConfig(x).config).changed === false across the whole fixture corpus
non-object roots (undefined / null / array / string / number / true) treated as {} — all keys filled, nothing thrown
empty catalog and catalog matching nothing → changed === false, config deep-equals existing
partially-present ancestor chain — intermediates synthesized, only the leaf recorded in filled, sibling keys untouched
ancestor segment collides with a scalar/array — subtree replaced, CATALOG path recorded in repaired with the discarded scalar value
value already exactly equal to the catalog default → carried, not filled
catalog row with an out-of-domain type throws ConfigCatalogError naming the offending path, never degrading to fill-default
catalog row whose own default fails its own declared type throws ConfigCatalogError naming the path
existing document is never mutated — deep-freeze helper input reconciles and deep-equals itself afterwards
